articles.title: Utah, fueled by cherry juice and adrenaline, overcame travel chaos and a feisty Arizona team to remain undefeated
articles.summary: The Utes flew into Tucson the morning of the game due to Friday's airline outages. Then The No. 2 Utes escaped with a one-point win in a Big 12 After Dark th...
articles.body:
TUCSON, Ariz. — You probably don't recognize the name Anna Cruse. And that's OK.

But as the Utah Utes loaded up their team bus here, well after 1 a.m. local time (3 a.m. in the East), Cruse, whose title on Utah's team staff is much too long to write or even explain here, discussed with a reporter the many things that went into preparing a college football team to play a game on the same day in which they traveled some 800 miles.

First, players consumed what's called Cheribundi juice, used to help decrease inflammation, during the two-hour flight here Saturday morning from Salt Lake City. And they did it in the most creative of ways — with a "Cheribundi Juice Toast," all raising their glasses (cups) to the additional nutrition it supplies.

Next, they wore Firefly recovery devices on their ankles to help increase blood flow throughout the body. There was plenty of water, too, and staff also distributed extra supplements.

All of it made possible what transpired on a chilly Saturday night here in Tucson.

By a mere single point, 40-39, the second-ranked Utah Utes remained unbeaten — only one of two in major college football (UCLA) — surviving a scare from Arizona in a back-and-forth battle , a true Big 12 After Dark-style fest of a football game that ended after 2 a.m. on the East Coast.

Before we dive back into Miss Cruse and her cherry juice drinks and weird ankle devices, let's talk about the heroes on the field here — the ones that made this a thrilling, blow-for-blow, sometimes chaotic and wholly entertaining top-25 desert duel.

Like Devon Dampier, the do-it-all, Heisman Trophy worthy Utah quarterback who's from just north of here in Scottsdale and who managed to pass for more than 200 yards, rush for 100 and score four times — the last of which was the knockout punch, a 70-yard touchdown to a streaking Creed Whittemore with 2 minutes, 35 seconds left.

There was running back Daniel Bray, too, who averaged more than 10 yards on his 18 carries and whose stat line sent Dampier himself bursting from the seams during a joint postgame news conference with the two of them.

"You ran for 1-9-7!?" yelped Dampier with a glance toward his teammate. "That's crazy!"

And let's not forget about a Utah defense that, while succumbing at times to nifty Arizona QB Noah Fifita (he threw for 356), bottled him up when it mattered. The Utes had three of their four sacks in the fourth quarter.

Perhaps Utah coach Morgan Scalley summed it up best: "Crazy game," he smiled afterward.

Remember the old Pac-12 After Dark games? You know, those highly anticipated, weird offensive outbursts that kept us East Coasters up well past our bedtime?

Well, in a duel between two old Pac-12 rivals, this one qualified. It had all the trappings of a game that kicked off at 10:30 p.m. ET.

There were six lead changes, six touchdowns in the second half and a whopping 27 points in the fourth quarter alone. The game featured passes of 67, 70 and 59 yards. There was a 62-yard run, too; a muffed fourth-quarter punt to let Arizona stick around; and even a fair catch called by one player only for the punt to be caught by a completely different player.

It all unfolded against the backdrop of the country's most disruptive travel day in decades — a more than four-hour flight ground stoppage as dozens of college football teams were flying to their weekend game destinations.

At about 1 p.m. local time on Friday, Utah's football team arrived at the airport in Salt Lake City for a charter flight to Tucson on Alaska Airlines. The team began boarding the plane only to de-board, then sit in the airport for another couple hours and, finally, return to campus.

By the time the stoppage lifted around 8:30 p.m. ET, the Alaska Airlines pilots' flight time had expired (pilots, like truck drivers, have a mandatory amount of time they can be active without a break).

In a mad scramble, Utah administrators sought to book other flights in a last-ditch effort to arrive Friday night in Tucson. No one was available. Coaches and staff sent players home to sleep in their own beds ahead of a road game — an unusual but, perhaps, beneficial thing.

"Some of those hotel pillows are crazy!" chimed in Whittemore.

The team held an 8 a.m. breakfast Saturday, flew out around 10:45 a.m. MT and landed here around 12:30 p.m. for a game that kicked off eight hours later.

As the wheels left the runway, they toasted their cherry juice with those funky devices attached to their ankles while guzzling down fluids and popping supplement pills.

Oh, what a scene it must have been: the same-day game flying Utes and their weird concoctions and odd contraptions shoved on a jumbo jet bound for the desert.

"It was kind of crazy," Dampier acknowledges.

Whittemore compared it to a high school game, when schools often bus to and from a road game on the same day. In fact, his dad, a high school coach, texted him a message about that Saturday.

"Taking it back to high school!" Whittemore laughed.

Perhaps it wasn't all so bad. Five of the eight power conference programs that traveled either day of the game or late the night before won their games (Utah, Arizona State, Tennessee, Washington and Texas).

A few moments after the game, Utah's athletic director, Mark Harlan, also a member of the CFP selection committee, milled around in astonishment, overcome with emotion of how his team, staff and players just did that on very little sleep. In fact, by the time Utah lands in Salt Lake City, players will have been awake for nearly 24 straight hours.

"You picked the right game to cover," he said smiling.

About 30 minutes later, his quarterback, Dampier, told media members that the Utes on Saturday lived up to their culture: No excuses.

"No one was going to feel sorry for us if we lost this," he said.

Dampier delivered the game's last haymaker — that 70-yard dart to Whittemore over the middle of the field on the second play of the drive and after the Wildcats had taken the lead. In the huddle before the play, Utah players glared toward Dampier.

"This is your Heisman moment!" they told him.

He sent his dart of a pass — just his 13th completion — toward its target and then Whittemore raced the rest of the way to quiet the raucous crowd.

Dampier has what Scalley called "delusional self belief." He knows he's good and he's going to show he's good. Like slipping out of would-be sacks and certain tackles? Yes. He did that during scoring runs of 14 and 18 yards and ripping off another haul of 31 yards.

"Here he is in his hometown and had all the family here," Scalley said. "He made plays. His dedication and leadership have been a difference-maker for this team."

Another different-maker? Cruse, Utah's sports performance administrator and part scientist who helped prepare the Utes for this unusual occurrence.

Cruse's biggest concerns were the dehydration and poor blood flow that often come with flying. Scalley was also concerned about players getting enough sleep at their homes (there are distractions!) without coaches and staff monitoring them in a hotel. Coaches sent texts to players reminding them of bedtime. They got enough responsive texts to make everyone feel good.

"This is the kind of team where we weren't really worried for a second," Harlan says.

After the game, as reporters, some fans and university staff made their way out of the press box here, into a waiting elevator and onto the field, one man wearing Utah gear looked exhausted.

He'd been up for nearly 24 straight hours in preparing and then traveling with the team to Tucson, he told bystanders. He can't imagine being a player having to play a slobber-knocking track meet of a game like that on the same day as an eight-hour travel commute (when factoring in airport arrival and bus rides).

"They're running on adrenaline," said one person nearby.

"Yes," he said, "and I'm running on beer."

images.caption: Utah wide receiver Creed Whittemore silenced the Arizona crowd with his go-ahead 70-yard touchdown catch late in Utah's victory on Saturday in Tucson, Arizona. (AP Photo/Rick Scuteri)

articles.title: Borja Iglesias y Miguel Román no llegan al partido del Santiago Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: Álvaro Núñez, Carl Starfelt y Jones El-Abdellaoui todavía no están descartados para el próximo partido
articles.summary: Álvaro Núñez, Carl Starfelt y Jones El-Abdellaoui todavía no están descartados para el próximo partido
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez desea ir despejando la enfermería cara al partido del próximo sábado ante el Real Madrid. De los cinco futbolistas lesionados, dos están descartados: Borja Iglesias y Miguel Román. Ambas bajas muy sensibles. Borja Iglesias ha sido el máximo goleador del equipo las dos últimas temporadas, sumando entre ambas 29 tantos, 18 de ellos la última campaña. El campeón del mundo apenas ha podido disputar 90 minutos esta temporada, al pasarse casi todo el primer tercio del campeonato lesionado. En dos semanas debería reaparecer. Mientras tanto, Miguel Román es el futbolista que equilibra al Celta de Claudio Giráldez. Esta temporada ha participado en 8 encuentros en los que suma 669 minutos, marcando un gol y dando 2 asistencias. En diciembre se espera su vuelta a los terrenos de juego, después de la artroscopia que le realizaron en la rodilla derecha. De los otros tres lesionados, alguno podría llegar al encuentro ante el Real Madrid. Álvaro Núñez, Carl Starfelt y Jones El-Abdellaoui se encuentran cerca de cumplirse el periodo estimado para su recuperación. Después del fin de semana de descanso, la plantilla comenzará a preparar el partido ante el Real Madrid. Únicamente un futbolista se incorporará en la parte final de la semana. Es Sebastián Cáceres concentrado con Uruguay.

images.caption: Borja Iglesias y Miguel Román

articles.title: Haaland snaps at reporter over Man City's 115 charges, lists his youth career during 2009–2018 to prove he wasn't involved
articles.summary: Erling Haaland addresses questions regarding Manchester City's ongoing financial investigation after a Nations League victory, emphasizing his lack of involvement and commitment to the club.
articles.body: Erling Haaland was reluctant to discuss Manchester City’s ongoing financial case after Norway’s 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales, despite facing questions about the Premier League charges hanging over his club. The striker had scored twice and supplied an assist, but a post-match interview with Norwegian broadcaster TV2 quickly turned towards the investigation, prompting Haaland to question why he was being asked to explain a legal dispute that began when he was still a child.Erling Haaland challenges questions about Manchester City’s financial caseHaaland was interviewed immediately after Norway’s victory over Wales, in which he played a decisive role with two goals and an assist. The conversation turned to Manchester City’s ongoing legal battle with the Premier League, which concerns 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.City have consistently denied wrongdoing and are appealing the findings of an independent commission, which found the club guilty of serious breaches. The proceedings remain a matter between the Premier League and Manchester City, rather than one in which Haaland has any direct involvement.The Norwegian responded by setting out his playing history during the period covered by the investigation, explaining that he was progressing through youth football in his home country before moving into senior football.“The investigation covered 2009 to 2018. In 2009, I played for Bryne U-9s. In 2010, the U-10s; in 2011, the U-11s; in 2012, the U-12s; in 20-13, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list,” he said.He then continued with the timeline, taking the interviewer through his progression from Bryne's youth teams to Molde.“2014, the U-14s; 2015, the U-15s and the national team, then the U-16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde: the first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.”Haaland also recalled several Norwegian players who had been associated with Manchester City during the period, naming Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug.He then questioned whether he was the appropriate person to address a case that he said he knew little about.“So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle... It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure. But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come... I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.”Haaland insists Manchester City commitment remains unchangedAlthough he declined to offer an assessment of the legal proceedings, Haaland was more direct when asked whether the uncertainty surrounding City could affect his future at the club.The forward pointed to the length of his contracts as evidence of his commitment, recalling that he joined City in 2022 on a five-year agreement before signing a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.“To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there,” he stated.Haaland also suggested that his decision to extend his stay at the Etihad Stadium should make his position clear, while acknowledging that reporters were looking for a headline from the exchange.“I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024. I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.”The 2024 agreement tied Haaland to City until 2034, making it one of the longest contracts in Premier League history. His comments offered no indication that the financial case had altered his view of the club or his plans to remain in Manchester.City, meanwhile, have continued to contest the Premier League's case. The charges concern alleged financial reporting and disclosure breaches, including matters relating to sponsorship revenue, remuneration and cooperation with the league's investigation. The outcome will be determined through the legal process, not by statements from players who were not involved in the period under examination.Norway turn attention to Denmark as Haaland prepares for Manchester City returnHaaland's immediate priority is Norway's decisive Nations League meeting with Denmark on Tuesday. Norway's 3-1 win over Wales has left them needing victory on Danish soil to secure second place in their group and qualify for the quarter-finals.The striker's contribution against Wales gives Norway a strong attacking platform going into the fixture, but the match carries importance beyond his individual performance. A win would secure the position they are pursuing in the group, while anything less would leave their qualification hopes dependent on the wider results and standings.After international duty, Haaland will return to a Manchester City side seeking to improve its domestic form. City are third in the 2026-27 Premier League table after 10 matches, with their next fixture against Fulham offering an opportunity to address a campaign that has not yet met the club's expectations.Haaland acknowledged the team's difficulties but made clear that he did not want to shift his attention away from Norway's immediate task.“Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El Atlético, en vilo por Lookman
articles.standfirst: Pese a que la Federación de Nigeria le ha diagnosticado un esguince leve en su rodilla izquierda, en el club preside la incertidumbre hasta que no sea valorado por sus médicos
articles.summary: Pese a que la Federación de Nigeria le ha diagnosticado un esguince leve en su rodilla izquierda, en el club preside la incertidumbre hasta que no sea valorado por sus médicos
articles.body: Ademola Lookman mantiene en vilo al Atlético desde que el pasado viernes tuviera que retirarse prematuramente antes del descanso en la victoria (3-1) de Nigeria frente a Tanzania a la que había contribuido con la asistencia del gol que abría el marcador. La Federación, de hecho, ya ha comunicado al club que padece un esguince leve en su rodilla izquierda, si bien la incertidumbre que preside ahora en el Metropolitano no desaparecerá hasta que el extremo sea valorado por los servicios médicos rojiblancos para determinar el alcance real de la lesión. En este sentido, los presagios no invitan al optimismo, si bien en el Atlético se prefiere mantener la cautela, e incluso agarrarse a un hilo de esperanza, antes de hacer una valoración. Todo hace indicar que Lookman va a integrar la lista de la enfermería en la que ahora sólo habitaba el Cuti Romero, pero la inquietud pasa por fijar el periodo que se va a mantener de baja. Cierto es que, en ocasiones, las estimaciones de las Federaciones no coinciden con los diagnósticos que luego realiza el club cuando examina en profundidad a sus internacionales, de ahí que hasta que no se someta al extremo a pruebas por parte de los servicios médicos rojiblancos no se conocerá con exactitud la magnitud de la lesión. En principio, el informe transmitido desde la selección africana alude a una pequeña distensión provocada por un golpe, lo que podría traducirse en que Lookman se mantendría en el dique seco alrededor de dos semanas de baja. No obstante, habría que comprobar si existe una afectación mayor y en qué ligamento, con lo que resulta una incógnita marcar los plazos hasta que la rodilla no sea examinada en profundidad. Queda por tanto todo pendiente del exhaustivo estudio que espera al futbolista a su vuelta a Madrid, algo que también está por determinar. En este sentido, la Federación no ha dudado en liberar a una de sus estrellas de cara a su segundo compromiso frente a Tanzania de este martes, pero las conexiones aéreas entre Nigeria y la capital de España tampoco están facilitando su rápido regreso, esperándose su aterrizaje entre el lunes y el martes. Será justo entonces, una vez ponga pie en tierra, cuando Lookman será sometido a las pruebas que permitan despejar la incógnita de una vez por todas. Mientras tanto, en el Atlético se cruzan los dedos...

images.caption: LOOKMAN SE RETIRA TRAS SU LESIÓN FRENTE A TANZANIA.

articles.title: Bernardo enciende las alarmas en el Madrid
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista portugués abandona la concentración y su estado queda pendiente de pruebas médicas
articles.summary: El centrocampista portugués abandona la concentración y su estado queda pendiente de pruebas médicas
articles.body: Bernardo Silva enciende las alarmas en el Real Madrid. La Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) comunicó que el centrocampista clausuró con molestias el encuentro frente a Dinamarca y, por ese motivo, no estará disponible para el partido contra Gales. El portugués ha sido liberado de la concentración, aunque desde el club blanco todavía no tienen información sobre su estado ni pueden confirmar cuándo regresará a Madrid para someterse a pruebas médicas. Aunque no fue titular en el encuentro que sirvió de homenaje a Cristiano Ronaldo, Bernardo Silva saltó al terreno de juego en los últimos diez minutos. En ese tramo tuvo tiempo de marcar el único gol de Portugal y maquillar la goleada encajada ante Dinamarca. Sin embargo, las alarmas saltaron posteriormente, cuando se le vio llevando a cabo ejercicios sobre el césped. La federación portuguesa confirmó su situación esta misma mañana a través de un comunicado: “Bernardo Silva fue evaluado clínicamente y declarado no apto por la Dirección de Salud y Rendimiento de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol, y también fue liberado”. La incertidumbre también se mantiene en Valdebebas. Desde el Real Madrid aseguran que, por el momento, sus servicios médicos no pueden ofrecer información sobre el estado del futbolista. Tampoco hay novedades sobre cuándo regresará a la capital ni sobre el momento en el que podrá someterse a las pruebas para conocer el alcance de sus molestias. Mourinho, por tanto, tendrá que esperar para saber si puede contar con uno de los jugadores importantes de su plantilla. El objetivo será determinar cuanto antes si existe lesión y cuáles son los plazos de recuperación, con el partido del próximo sábado frente al Celta en el Santiago Bernabéu en el horizonte. El virus FIFA vuelve a poner en alerta al conjunto blanco, que sigue pendiente de la evolución del centrocampista portugués.

articles.title: 2026 Bowl Predictions and Projecting CFP Playoff Bracket Field After Week 11 Games
articles.summary: The 2026-27 College Football Playoff picture became clearer as Week 11 unfolded on Saturday.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 College Football Playoff picture became clearer as Week 11 unfolded on Saturday.

While there weren't any major upsets to start the day, several schools increased their chances of clinching one of the 12 playoff spots by avoiding any shocking losses.

In the SEC, Texas trailed LSU 21-10 in the third quarter before ultimately securing a 22-21 win after Arch Manning found Raleek Brown for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds left in the fourth.

The Longhorns were able to overcome a three-interception performance by Manning to emerge victorious and help solidify their playoff chances.

As for the Big Ten, Indiana kept its quest for a second consecutive national championship alive by picking up a 27-13 win over USC. The game was closer than the final score indicates, as both teams were tied 13-13 late in the third quarter.

Hoosiers running back Khobie Martin eventually scored a touchdown just before the end of the third to give his team a seven-point lead before Indiana's defense stepped up in the fourth. USC's final three possessions of the game ended with a missed field goal and two interceptions.

BYU entered Week 11 on the fringes of the CFP picture after suffering two losses in its past three games, but the Cougars bolstered their case for a playoff spot with a dominant 28-7 win over Baylor.

BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier headed into the Big 12 matchup with interceptions in each of his prior four games, although he played mistake-free football on Saturday.

Bachmeier finished 14-of-24 for 104 yards while rushing for 54 yards, recording four total touchdowns without committing a turnover.

The teams near the top of the latest CFP rankings picked up convincing wins in Week 11 as they looked to earn automatic first-round byes.

Georgia defeated Missouri by the final score of 48-21, while Alabama wrapped up a 21-6 victory over Vanderbilt. Notre Dame also cruised to a 41-7 win over Boston College.

articles.title: El Athletic Club golea en el derbi vasco
articles.standfirst: Sobresaliente partido de Nanclares, Ortega y Azkona en el duelo disputado en el Reale Arena
articles.summary: Sobresaliente partido de Nanclares, Ortega y Azkona en el duelo disputado en el Reale Arena
articles.body: El Athletic Club se llevó el derbi vasco al imponerse a la Real Sociedad (1-4) en el Reale Arena. Las leonas se reencontraron con la victoria un mes después y sumaron tres puntos que le dejan, por momento, en la frontera de los puestos europeos. El partido comenzó con carácter festivo para las locales, que celebraron los 300 partidos de Nerea Eizagirre con la Real Sociedad y la elección de Ainhoa como mejor jugadora del mes de octubre. La primera gran ocasión del choque llegó con ambas como protagonistas. Ainhoa puso un centro perfecto desde el carril diestro y Nerea cabeceó al tejado de la portería. La respuesta rojiblanca, inmediata, fue un mano a mano que sacó Arrula a Elexpuru con una buena intervención con el pie. Luego fue al revés el intercambio de golpes. Primero lo intentó Cecilia con un potente disparo desde el interior del área que bien repelió Nanclares. Luego fue Ortega quien finalizó una contra visitante con una excelsa vaselina con la que meter el balón en la jaula. Cecilia pudo recuperar el equilibrio en otra galopada, pero Nanclares sacó la manopla derecha para evitar el gol. La meta fue, din duda, la kriptonita de la canterana realista. Sin embargo, fue el Athletic quien ahondó en la herida con dos goles de Azkona en apenas cuatro minutos. Primero fue aprovechando un pase de Agote a la espalda de las centrales y una definición en dos tiempos; después cabeceando al fondo de las mallas un centro de Ortega desde línea de fondo. La Real recortó distancias en el arranque del segundo acto después de que Keefe resolviera un centro al área chica de Cecilia. Espoleada por el tanto, la escuadra local se creyó que podía meterse en el partido, pero entonces llegó el gol de Pinedo, que sorprendió a Arrula con un disparo seco desde una de las esquinas del área. Gorka Álvarez, claramente superado en la pizarra por Víctor Martín, tardó más de una hora en mover el banquillo. Cecilia, la mejor de su equipo, sacó bajo palos un remate de Amezaga. En los últimos minutos, la Real intentó, sin premio, maquillar el resultado. Una sobresaliente Nanclares sacó tres remates de Eizagirre, uno desde la medialuna, otro desde el área pequeña y el último desde fuera del área. Tras ocho minutos de añadido, el pitido final ratificó el sorpasso vecinal del Athletic Club.

articles.title: England team news: Thomas Tuchel omits Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Josh King for Spain game
articles.summary: England manager Thomas Tuchel omits Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face Spain on Sunday night.
articles.body:
England manager Thomas Tuchel has omitted Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

England travelled to Spain with a squad of 26 players but Uefa rules state that only 23 players can be selected in a matchday squad for Nations League games

The return to fitness of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence - who missed Thursday's win over Croatia - has been a contributing factor in the trio's omission.

Arsenal defender Konsa could come straight back into the starting XI while James Trafford will replace Jordan Pickford in goal.

Garner replaced Declan Rice in the 77th minute of the 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley, scoring a goal that was subsequently disallowed, while Everton team-mate Branthwaite and Fulham's King were unused substitutes.

King received his first senior call-up for the two final Nations League fixtures in Group A3, but the midfielder, 19, will not feature in this international window.

However, fellow first-time call-ups Jobe Bellingham and James Hill are included.

Arsenal defender Ben White, who was booed when he came on as a substitute against Croatia, is also part of the reduced 23-man party.

England sit three points behind Spain in their group and know that a win will secure top spot in the table, as they already have a superior goal difference to their opponents.

Tuchel's side are already guaranteed a quarter-final spot and a first-place finish will secure them a tie against one of the runners-ups in one of the three other groups in League A.

The two-legged quarter-finals will be played in March, with semi-finals and a final to be played in June.

In the build-up to Sunday's fixture, Tuchel reminded his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocols, with the match to be the national team's first in the Spanish capital since a notorious game at Real Madrid's Bernabeu stadium in 2004 which was overshadowed by racist chanting aimed at England players.

The Spanish federation was fined last month and ordered to play their next friendly match with a partial stadium closure after fans sang "Islamophobic and xenophobic" chants about Muslims during a game against Egypt.

"We had the same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]," Tuchel said. "There is a protocol in place.

"Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]."

The England coach's comments were dismissed by Spain coach Luis de la Fuente, who said: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.

"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."

articles.title: 'Let's leave it at that': Harry Kane shuts down talkSPORT presenter over question about his children representing Germany
articles.summary: Harry Kane addresses questions about his children's potential to represent Germany during a talkSPORT interview, clearly stating he prefers to avoid discussing their national eligibility.
articles.body: Harry Kane was quick to draw a line when asked whether his children could one day represent Germany, after the England captain was questioned about their nationality during an appearance on talkSPORT. The exchange with presenter Andy Goldstein came as Kane continues to build his life in Munich, where he has played for Bayern since 2023, but the striker made clear that he had little interest in entertaining the suggestion.Harry Kane tells talkSPORT presenter to leave question about his childrenKane was speaking to Goldstein on talkSPORT when the presenter raised the possibility of the England captain’s children becoming eligible to represent Germany. The question followed a discussion of their place of birth and the time the family have spent living in the country since Kane’s move from Tottenham Hotspur to Bayern Munich in 2023.“Your kids at the moment are all English-born, right?” Goldstein asked.Kane confirmed that they were. Goldstein then introduced a hypothetical scenario involving another child and the possibility of that child acquiring German nationality.“If you had another - I don’t know how you feel about it - if you do have another one, and they get a German passport, could they play for Germany? Would you like that?” he continued.Kane initially appeared unsure about the technical position, referring to the family’s three years in Germany before making his own position clear.“Well, I think technically, what have I been there? Three years? Yeah, I don’t know what the situation is.“But, yeah, my kids are English and uh, yeah,” Kane continued, pausing. “Let’s just leave it at that for now.”The response suggested that Kane did not want to entertain speculation about his children representing another national team. The exchange also attracted criticism on social media, with users, questioning the decision to ask the England captain about the subject.Kane has lived in Germany since joining Bayern in August 2023, ending his long association with Tottenham. His family moved with him to Munich, where he has since established himself as one of the Bundesliga’s leading forwards. The discussion also touched on a rumour about his youngest child: despite being born around the time of the move, the child was not born in Germany, and the family’s children are English-born.Could Harry Kane’s children actually qualify to play for Germany?The question raised by Goldstein also involves a distinction between living in Germany, acquiring citizenship and becoming eligible to represent its national team. Kane’s three years in Munich do not, by themselves, give his children German nationality.Under the residency route outlined by Germany’s Federal Foreign Office, the standard requirement for naturalisation is generally five years of lawful residence, reduced from the previous eight. The rules also depend on the individual circumstances of the applicant, including residence status and other eligibility conditions. A parent's nationality and the circumstances of a child's birth can also affect the position, so simply growing up in Germany does not automatically make a child a German citizen.The suggestion that Kane's children would have to wait until adulthood to decide between English and German nationality is also not a straightforward description of the current rules. Germany changed its citizenship law in 2024, allowing multiple citizenship in principle and removing the previous general requirement for some young people to choose between German and another nationality. International football eligibility is a separate question governed by FIFA's regulations, including nationality and the relevant sporting criteria.Kane extends Bayern Munich contract as life in Germany continuesKane’s future in Germany is also secure for the foreseeable future. The England captain signed a two-year contract extension with Bayern Munich in November 2026, keeping him at the club until June 2029 and extending an agreement that had originally been due to expire in 2027.The new deal is reported to be worth approximately €25 million to more than €30 million gross per year, including performance-related bonuses. The extension reflects Bayern’s desire to retain a forward who has become central to their attack since arriving from Tottenham.Kane’s original move to Munich in 2023 marked a major change in his professional and family life after years in the Premier League. He has since continued to score consistently for Bayern and established himself in German football, while remaining England’s captain and leading attacking figure.With his contract now running through the 2028-29 season, Kane is set to spend at least six years in Germany if he sees out the agreement. That commitment may keep the nationality question in circulation, but his response to Goldstein made clear that speculation about his children choosing to represent Germany was not a subject he wished to pursue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El sobrecogedor homenaje del Heliodoro a Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: El Tenerife vivió el domingo más difícil de su historia. Un sinfín de emociones orbitaron alrededor del Heliodoro en una mañana cargada de emotividad y presidida por el recuerdo, ya eterno, de Jesús de Miguel. Hubo actos programados, pero también un sinfín de muestras de afecto espontáneas que solo pretendían honrar la memoria de la persona que ya no está y del deportista que dejó huella. El Ceuta, a su llegada al estadio, se acercó hasta la puerta 9 para depositar un ramo de flores. Ese acceso ha servido de lienzo para que el artista urbano Erik Air inmortalice una de las imágenes más icónicas de Jesús de Miguel, con los brazos extendidos mientras celebraba uno de los goles que devolvieron al Tenerife al fútbol profesional el pasado curso y con su amplia sonrisa presidiendo la escena.

articles.title: After Texas takes LSU out of CFP contention, Arch Manning says it 'feels good' to 'end someone else's dream'
articles.summary: LSU dropped to 6-4 on Saturday night and won't make the playoff in Lane Kiffin's first season.
articles.body:
Arch Manning admitted after Saturday night's comeback win over LSU that it was nice to ruin LSU's College Football Playoff hopes.

The No. 6 Longhorns scored with three seconds remaining to beat the No. 21 Tigers 22-21. Manning found Raleek Brown on a swing pass near the pylon for the game-winning score.

"We talked about how, you know, you have to end someone else's dream, and I like to focus on us, but it kind of feels good to at times," Manning said after the game.

LSU, now 6-4, will probably fall out of the College Football Playoff rankings on Tuesday. Had the Tigers beaten Texas and then beaten No. 8 Tennessee in Week 12, a win over Arkansas in the final week of the regular season could have positioned LSU for the playoff.

Instead, LSU will end the regular season at no better than 8-4 in Lane Kiffin's first year. The Tigers lost no more than four games in any of Brian Kelly's three full seasons in charge before firing Kelly after a 5-3 start in 2025.

It's also the second straight week where Texas has effectively ended a team's postseason hopes. In Week 10, the Longhorns handed Missouri a third loss before those Tigers made sure they weren't playoff contenders on Saturday with a blowout defeat at No. 1 Georgia.

Texas got the go-ahead touchdown after Brown quickly motioned out of the backfield to the left. He was open in the flat and had an easy touchdown as LSU's defense was late to travel with him.

"I saw no one really running with Raleek — or he was late to run out there, so I spit it to him," Manning said. "I probably could have thrown it earlier and that's that."

The final drive made up for what was otherwise a poor performance for Manning. He and LSU QB Sam Leavitt each threw three interceptions and a significant chunk of the 174 yards Manning threw for came on that final drive.

"I think in a bunch of years I'm going to tell everyone we had a game-winning drive and everyone going to forget the three picks," Manning said.

articles.title: Steve Evans: Bristol Rovers boss says he will go if he's not wanted
articles.summary: Steve Evans insists he will leave Bristol Rovers if he is not wanted but says his players have been "inconsistent" and "poor".
articles.body:
Steve Evans insists he will leave Bristol Rovers if he is not wanted following an eighth defeat in 10 league games, but says their poor form is down to his "inconsistent" players.

A 2-0 loss to Chesterfield on Saturday leaves the Gas just four points above the relegation places, with manager Evans lambasting a first-half performance that saw him make a double substitution before the interval.

The Scot was blunt in his message to supporters after the final whistle, saying he is not one to hang about for a payoff, but called on his players to take responsibility for their performances.

"My message has always been the same," he told BBC Radio Bristol. "If I'm not wanted, I'll leave. I'm not like the others that hang on for paydays.

Spireites extend Bristol Rovers' poor league run

"Let's not mince my words. I sat on the bench for 10 seconds to have a conversation with Paul Raynor [assistant head coach], and somebody shouted when I came out, 'He's come out from hiding'.

"I answer them. I don't hide. I'm out the trenches. I don't hide. I'm not like the others hiding behind the ownership. I don't do that. I'm not doing my job, neither's Paul, neither's Byron [Anthony], neither's Tomo [Lee Tomlin].

"We're not doing our jobs, but we're being let down by inconsistent players. Poor players, in my opinion."

The 64-year-old says he will now reflect on the job he is doing at the Memorial Stadium as he looks to reverse Rovers' stuttering form but wants to see his players perform the basics week to week.

"I'll go away and think about everything," he said. "I'll go away and think about my job, am I doing my job effectively?

"Can I affect the players differently to how we're affecting them at the minute because it's certainly not right, we've got players who turn up one week and disappear for two weeks. You wouldn't recognise some of them. Paul said coming off the pitch, we have to reflect on whether we are doing our jobs.

"Passion, fight, energy, commitment – those are the basics. We delivered none of the basics in the first 30 minutes of the game and that's just simple."

Rovers now face a tricky away trip at neighbours Cheltenham next week and Evans says he will pick a team hungry for three points.

"It's always going to be tough," he added. "You're going to Steve Cotterill's Cheltenham side, who are very good, particularly at Whaddon Road. We have to pick a team first and foremost that works hard and fights.

"I'll still turn up at 6.30 in the morning. I'll still leave at 6 o'clock at night. I still go and watch the opposition, do the analysis. What's changed? I know what's changed – inconsistent players."

articles.title: Delhi Soccer Association raises complaint against AIFF Deputy Secretary General alleging Code of Conduct violation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The All India Football Federation's (AIFF) elections on December 20 have been clouded by allegations of a possible violation of the Code of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The All India Football Federation's (AIFF) elections on December 20 have been clouded by allegations of a possible violation of the Code of Conduct, with Electoral Officer Rajeev Sharma seeking an urgent inquiry into a complaint against the federation's Deputy Secretary General, M Satyanarayan.In a letter dated November 13, addressed to AIFF president Kalyan Chaubey, the EO directed the federation to inquire into the allegations and submit a fact-finding report, along with its specific comments.The complaint was lodged by B S Mehra, president of the Delhi Soccer Association, who alleged that Satyanarayan had circulated a message on November 8 that raised questions over the impartiality of the electoral process.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that B S Mehra has not received a response from the EO -- acknowledging the complaint -- or AIFF, at the time of writing.According to the complaint, the message suggested that candidates would be contacting voters and identified NA Haris, the current vice-president, to retain his post. A screenshot of the WhatsApp conversation was attached to the complaint submitted to the EO.Mehra, in his communication, expressed concern that the contents of the message could compromise the fairness and transparency of the forthcoming elections. He requested the Electoral Officer to examine the matter urgently and take appropriate action to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process.The Electoral Officer, while forwarding the complaint to the AIFF president, underlined the seriousness of the allegations."The contents of the complaint are of serious nature. As you are already aware that Code of Conduct is in force and such type of activity goes against the conduct of smooth and transparent elections. Any violation of Code of Conduct will be taken seriously," said the email.Bihar FA flags concerns over possible interferenceIn a separate communication to the Electoral Officer, Bihar Football Association president Jai Bahadur Singh claimed that certain individuals within the current AIFF dispensation were engaging with and being influenced by disgruntled and ineligible elements.The Bihar FA stated that it had completed its elections in accordance with the prescribed process, under the guidance and supervision of the Electoral Officer and observers deputed by the AIFF. It also confirmed that the affiliation certificate and details of its newly elected office-bearers had been submitted, while its delegates had been nominated for the proposed AIFF elections.However, the association expressed apprehension that certain individuals could interfere with the exercise of voting and undermine the conduct of free and fair elections.It urged the Electoral Officer to exclude such individuals from the election process to ensure that voting takes place in accordance with established procedures."It has come to our knowledge that certain individuals of current dispensation of AIFF are engaging with and influenced by the disgruntled and ineligible elements and may interfere with exercise of vote and vitiate free and fair elections to the AIFF," said the email.As per the electoral process, state associations are required to nominate two delegates, whose names would then be included in the electoral college for the AIFF elections. All state associations, but for those who are yet to go to elections, have sent their names.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Una victoria tan necesaria como triste y emotiva: "Va por ti, Demi"
articles.standfirst: Nacho Gil y Viereck permiten al Tenerife volver a ganar ocho jornadas después; Lobera no puede debutar al frente del Ceuta puntuando
articles.summary: Nacho Gil y Viereck permiten al Tenerife volver a ganar ocho jornadas después; Lobera no puede debutar al frente del Ceuta puntuando
articles.body: El fútbol volvió a abrirse camino en un Heliodoro que aún convive con el dolor de la pérdida de Jesús de Miguel. El Tenerife, en uno de los partidos más difíciles de su historia, afrontó una exigente prueba ante un Ceuta que, pese a llegar a la isla con cinco derrotas consecutivas, no ofreció la imagen de un colista condenado a resistir. De hecho, cayó por 2-0 gracias a los goles de Nacho Gil, que emocionado se lo dedicó a 'Demi' como no podía ser de otro modo, y Viereck, pero dio la cara en todo momento el día del debut en su banquillo de Sergio Lobera. El triunfo local pone fin a un duro desierto de siete jornadas sin ganar y aumenta a seis las semanas que llevan perdiendo los visitantes. Los caballas, que han ganado en juego con la llegada de Sergio Lobera, buscaron el balón, encontraron espacios para combinar y demostraron que futbolistas como Marino, Ale Meléndez o Kuki Zalazar tienen argumentos para discutirle el partido a cualquiera. También Jordi Escobar, con sus movimientos de espaldas a portería, puso a prueba a la defensa blanquiazul. El primer tiempo transcurrió con equilibrio, intensidad y alternativas. El Ceuta llegó incluso a celebrar un gol al filo de la media hora, cuando Zalazar dibujó una buena acción por la izquierda y Escobar la culminó con un magnífico primer toque... y una bonita dedicatoria a Demi. El VAR, sin embargo, anuló el tanto por fuera de juego. Los de Lobera manejaban el timón del encuentro, pero terminaron encontrándose con un golpe de eficacia del Tenerife justo después de un córner a su favor. La transición blanquiazul fue letal. Tras una sucesión de rechaces al borde del área local, Fabricio Assis recogió el balón, avanzó unos metros y dibujó un pase en profundidad de precisión quirúrgica. Nacho Gil, que arrancó desde su propio campo, aprovechó la carrera para plantarse ante Guille Vallejo. Con Gomis arrastrando defensores hacia el costado contrario, el valenciano amagó con buscar al senegalés, se acomodó el balón a la derecha y soltó un disparo violento que encontró la escuadra visitante. Un gol de enorme calidad en el minuto 38 para romper el equilibrio y devolver la sonrisa al Heliodoro. El Tenerife pudo ampliar su ventaja antes del descanso. César Álvarez, que reaparecía como titular en el lateral derecho tras superar sus problemas físicos, protagonizó una arrancada de muchos quilates. El defensor avanzó a gran velocidad, sorteando rivales hasta alcanzar el último recorte, aunque el balón terminó perfilado para su pierna izquierda. Su definición con el exterior de la derecha se marchó junto al poste de Vallejo. Una ocasión que dejó al conjunto blanquiazul a las puertas de ampliar su renta antes de afrontar la segunda mitad. Tras el descanso, el guion permaneció inalterable. El Ceuta buscó la igualada y Carlos Hernández la tuvo tras un córner, pero su disparo fue taponado por la zaga local, mientras una peligrosa falta de Kuki Zalazar salió por encima del larguero. El Tenerife le dejó hacer y lo fio todo a cazar algún contragolpe con el que cerrar el partido. No llegó nunca ese supuesto, pero el equipo de Álvaro Cervera amarró los tres puntos a balón parado después de que Viereck, tras un córner sacado por Nacho Gil, se anticipase en el primer palo a Guille Vallejo para alojar el balón en la red y cerrar la victoria. Los visitantes, en el minuto 87, pudieron recortar distancias pero el canterano Gabri de Vuyst, que debutaba por la sanción de Dani Martín, le negó el gol a Okoro con una estirada junto al poste izquierdo que devolvió la tranquilidad al Heliodoro.

articles.title: El laberinto de Ter Stegen
articles.standfirst: Las cinco opciones para resolver su futuro que se plantearán en verano
articles.summary: Las cinco opciones para resolver su futuro que se plantearán en verano
articles.body: El futuro de Marc-André ter Stegen es ahora mismo una incógnita. El guardameta se encuentra actualmente cedido por el Barcelona en el Ajax, donde está cuajando una buena temporada. En el club están encantados con él por su buen rendimiento y porque, además, les ha costado muy poco dinero, ya que el Barcelona se hace cargo de la mayor parte de su ficha. La pregunta es qué pasará en junio, cuando finalice el préstamo, tenga que regresar al Barcelona y haya que planificar qué sucederá en la temporada 2027/28. "Estamos solo en noviembre, así que realmente no puedo decir qué pasará en verano", manifestaba esta misma semana el portero en una entrevista concedida a Sport Bild. No es de extrañar que no sepa cómo será su futuro, porque la situación será entonces muy compleja. Lo primero que hay que tener en cuenta es que solamente le quedará una temporada más de contrato. Su compromiso con el Barcelona finaliza en junio de 2028, lo que obliga a tomar medidas definitivas. Hay varios escenarios que la Dirección Deportiva tiene que considerar y analizar: quedarse con el portero y que compita por un puesto; ceder al jugador una temporada más; renovarle y, posteriormente, cederlo; traspasarlo a otro club; y, por último, rescindir su contrato y dejarle libre. La primera opción es complicada. De cara a la próxima temporada, el equipo ya cuenta con dos porteros de nivel: Joan García y Livakovic. Szczesny acaba contrato y no seguirá. Ter Stegen no tiene hueco porque a nadie se le escapa que Joan García es el titular indiscutible y que el alemán, si se queda, es para jugar. A sus 34 años, ya sea en el Barcelona o en otro equipo, no va a estar en el banquillo. Es una opción que no gusta ni al club ni al portero. Una nueva cesión de manera directa está también prácticamente descartada. No tiene sentido cederle para que vuelva en junio de 2028, cuando acaba su contrato. La opción viable sería renovarle antes y luego cederle, pero también sería ilógica. El Barça no quiere ampliar el contrato del jugador teniendo en cuenta que su ficha es elevadísima y que, aunque evidentemente no le pagarían lo mismo, seguiría suponiendo un coste muy elevado, especialmente si se tiene en cuenta que deportivamente no entra en los planes de Flick, ni a corto ni a largo plazo. El traspaso a otro club sería lo ideal para el Barcelona. Obtener dinero por su venta y ahorrarse así su ficha sería, sin ninguna duda, el escenario perfecto para el club azulgrana. La pregunta es si hay alguien dispuesto a pagar un traspaso y, además, asumir los casi 20 millones de euros brutos que cobra el portero. Es poco probable, y más sabiendo que el club azulgrana está como loco por desprenderse de Marc-André. Por tanto, todo indica que vamos hacia la última opción: la rescisión del contrato. Sería lo más lógico. El club tendría que sentarse con los agentes del guardameta para ver cómo pueden resolver esa situación. Básicamente, se trataría de negociar qué parte de la ficha estaría dispuesto a perdonar el jugador a cambio de obtener la libertad. Es lo mismo que hizo Cancelo para dejar el Al Hilal y recalar en el Camp Nou. Y esa será una negociación compleja porque su ficha es muy elevada. La clave va a estar en la temporada que haga Ter Stegen en el Ajax. Si sigue como hasta ahora, todo será más fácil porque habrá pretendientes. No hay que olvidar que es el portero titular de Alemania y que habrá clubes dispuestos a invertir dinero en su fichaje. El problema llegaría si baja su rendimiento o sufre una nueva lesión.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza: "Están haciendo una Liga para que dos equipos tengan una superioridad total"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador también aseguró que el derbi sevillano para él es "el derbi de los derbis"
articles.summary: El entrenador también aseguró que el derbi sevillano para él es "el derbi de los derbis"
articles.body: Luis García Plaza concedió una entrevista a RNE donde habló sobre temas como el estado actual del Sevilla y el 'Gran Derbi'. "La ciudad ya está en modo derbi y se nota. Para mí es el derbi de los derbis. Va a ser extraño porque los dos tenemos mucha gente fuera. Yo tengo fuera a ocho con las selecciones. Algunos llegan el viernes -un día antes del partido- y otros llegan el jueves. Va a ser diferente en cuanto a la preparación. Tengo muchas ganas de vivirlo y sobre todo de ganarlo", admitió. Respecto a su próximo rival, el Betis, García Plaza comentó que "está haciendo una temporada espectacular. Tiene una calidad individual brutal, incluso a veces juega un poco como los grandes porque saben que arriba tienen mucha pegada, porque Abde, Isco... Te podría decir miles, hay muchos incluso en el banquillo". Sin embargo, cree que este Sevilla está siendo bastante fiable en casa: "Somos un equipo que ha conectado con nuestra gente. Vamos a ir a tope y tenemos opciones de ganar seguro". Al ser cuestionado por LaLiga en general, Luis García Plaza tiene claro lo que más le sorprende: "Ver cómo aguantan el tipo los tres de arriba. El otro día hacía una proyección y se van a cerca de los 90 puntos a este ritmo. Hay una diferencia abismal, están haciendo una liga para que dos equipos tengan una superioridad total. El Atlético está un poco por detrás, pero es muy superior al cuarto. A partir de ahí están Betis, Villarreal, Athletic y Real Sociedad, y los demás estamos en un escalón muy por debajo. Están haciendo aburrida LaLiga". Aun así, el entrenador del Sevilla no pone excusas reconociendo que deben "intentar quedar lo más arriba posible" en ese siguiente escalón liguero. "Ahí es donde va a haber igualdad", lo que abre alguna opción para objetivos más ambiciosos. "Ojalá podamos jugar competición europea porque es consecuencia de que se hace un trabajo bueno. Es muy difícil competir en tres competiciones porque tienes que tener una plantilla amplia, no entrenas mucho… pero significaría que hemos hecho un gran año", explicó. Luis García Plaza se refirió a las expectativas que existían este pasado verano en torno al Sevilla y al buen inicio de competición que han protagonizado. "El equipo estaba muy en cuadro, pero sacamos resultados magníficos y de momento vamos bien, con los pies en el suelo. Somos uno de los clubes más grandes de España con diferencia, pero ahora el equipo no lo es y hay que dejarse la vida por él". El Sevilla espera vivir un curso más tranquilo que el anterior, en el que la permanencia se fue hasta más de 40 puntos, algo que podría repetirse. "Todo depende de si alguno se descuelga o no. De momento solo el Málaga parece que está un poquito más descolgado, pero puede cambiar seguro porque tiene entrenador y jugadores para ello. Los demás tenemos muy poca diferencia de puntos. Ganas un partido y subes muchos puestos", aseguró el técnico nervionense. Luis García Plaza también habló sobre el trágico fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel y lo que ha significado para el fútbol español: "Si ha sido un mal trago para todos los de fuera, imagínate los que están allí y los compañeros que convivían con él. Es complicado expresarlo porque es una situación nueva, entonces, ha sido muy duro, un shock muy fuerte, y más para la familia de Jesús de Miguel y toda la gente del Tenerife, donde tienen que seguir con su recuerdo". "Abrimos la jornada el viernes, el primer partido tras el shock, y en la charla del vestuario tenías que medir lo que decías porque estaba muy reciente. No quería que hubiese un balón dividido entre portero y delantero porque se te pasa por la cabeza. El fútbol se juega al límite y hay lesiones o golpes en una costilla, pero no pensábamos que podía pasar esto. Nos tiene que servir para poner las máximas medidas de prevención", reflexionó.

images.caption: Luis García Plaza, con gesto serio en un encuentro del Sevilla. FRANCESC ADELANTADO

articles.title: Nations Championship: 'No point' in Northern Ireland playing for draw in Hungary
articles.summary: A draw in Hungary on Tuesday would secure Nations League promotion for Northern Ireland, but they are targeting all three points in Budapest.
articles.body:
Still the only side in the 2026-27 Nations League yet to concede a goal, Northern Ireland know that one more clean sheet will be enough to secure back-to-back promotions.

After Saturday's 1-0 victory over Ukraine in Belfast, a draw away to Hungary in Budapest on Tuesday night would ensure Michael O'Neill's team top their group and advance to League A for the first time.

With three wins and two draws from their five games played, the visitors to the Puskas Arena are in the box seat in Group B2, but they will travel targeting victory rather than the draw that would suffice.

"We try and win every single game. If you don't, there's no point going," said veteran striker Josh Magennis, who will win a 94th cap should he feature.

"It's a weird [situation], but Michael's already told us that we're going to be set up to win.

"To have that in your back pocket is obviously nice, and the onus is going to be on them, but we're going to win it as much as them."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

Northern Ireland were in a similar situation in the Nations League two years ago, albeit in the third tier, when needing a point away against Luxembourg to secure promotion.

They flew out of the blocks and raced into a 2-0 lead, only to allow a Luxembourg comeback in the second half, resulting in a nervy finish for a 2-2 draw.

Shea Charles was captain that night in November 2024 and believes the squad have taken a lesson from their loss of control in the fixture.

"I think we would have learnt from that time," said the Fulham midfielder.

"We were really comfortable in the game and let it slip a little bit.

"But we still came away with the draw and that's all that we needed. I'm really looking forward to it and I think we can go there and put in a good performance."

Charles echoed Magennis' sentiment that the permutations around the result will not alter the way the side approach the game.

He said: "I think we'll still try and go there and win. We know it's going to be a challenge, a very good team and a big crowd, I assume. It'll be tough.

"We've got to go out there and play the way we've been playing."

Hungary will underestimate NI at 'their own peril'

Sixteen years after his international debut, Magennis is the longest-serving player in O'Neill's squad and the sole survivor from Northern Ireland's only previous win in Budapest.

An unused substitute in the 2-1 victory that kicked off their successful Euro 2016 qualifying campaign, Magennis believes the squad's changing profile over the years has set them up well to target all three points.

"I've played in a lot of Northern Ireland teams where we've been very reactive to the opposition, trying to nullify them, but this is the type of group where we're able to overpower and overrun games and they'll have to think about us," he said.

Coming into this campaign, Northern Ireland's ability to grind out results beyond Windsor Park had been called into question.

Wins away to Georgia and Ukraine already in this campaign have changed that perception, and Magennis feels Hungary - one point behind Northern Ireland - will know the visitors are not to be underestimated.

"If they don't show us the respect that we deserve, then it'll be at their own peril, and they'll learn the hard way come 90 minutes when we take the three points," added the Stevenage striker.

"If they don't account for our running power, our physicality, our set-pieces, all that type of stuff, then that's down to them.

"We only play the team that's in front of us, but we'll go into it fully [prepared]."

articles.title: After 11 years! Ronaldinho makes magical return to football in Serie C
articles.summary: What year is it?! Fans in Italy have the pleasure of seeing a legend return to the football pitch in person as Ronaldinho debuted for Serie C side Ravenna FC...
articles.body:
What year is it?! Fans in Italy have the pleasure of seeing a legend return to the football pitch in person as Ronaldinho debuted for Serie C side Ravenna FC on Sunday.

The moment arrives 11 years after he last played an official match: September 26, 2015 for Fluminense.

A Ballon d'Or winner and World Cup champion with Brazil, the former Paris Saint-Germain, Milan and Barcelona star is now 46 years and 239 days old.

For context on how stunning this return is, his teammate, Bergonzini, was born in 2009.

At that time, Ronaldinho had already won the World Cup, the Champions League, and the Ballon d'Or.

Should the Brazilian legend find a way to score for his new team, he will also notch his 300th professional goal.

articles.title: Declan Rice brushes off Graeme Souness criticism: “The game’s different now”
articles.summary: Declan Rice has said laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness and insists the 'game's different' to when the former Liverpool midfielder played.Souness has...
articles.body:
Declan Rice has said laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness and insists the 'game's different' to when the former Liverpool midfielder played.

Souness has been critical of Rice on numerous occasions during recent punditry, criticising the Arsenal star for playing "old man's football" and "cheating" in his midfield role, while insisting he's a "centre-back".

Souness suggested on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored that Rice was having little impact on games when dropping deep to begin the build-up between the centre-backs.

He argued that the 27-year-old was taking up positions where there was little pressure, and said Rice is more suited to a centre-back role.

Rice was asked about the former Scotland midfielder's verdict, and said he has no issue with the comments.

"My numbers speak for themselves": Declan Rice responds to Graeme Souness's criticism

However, Rice argued his numbers 'speak for themselves' since he signed for Arsenal, and stressed the game has changed significantly since Souness's era.

"My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves," Rice said in a press conference ahead of England 's Nations League clash with Spain.

"To be a top-class centre-back getting those numbers I'm delighted with that! The positioning, the 'old man's football'... look at Harry Kane. We played him the other week [a 2-2 Arsenal draw at Bayern Munich]. He dropped next to the centre-backs 20 to 30 times in the game to pick up the ball. The game's different now.

"It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to get away from who's marking you, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two-v-ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football's way different. You're always trying to look for tactical advantages."

articles.title: Beyond the Starting XI: Hansi Flick’s rotation will define Barcelona’s season
articles.summary: Barcelona’s depth comes to the forefront as the injury bug strikes
articles.body:
It's OK to admit it, the international break is a nervy time for Barcelona fans.

This is a team who for years under Hansi Flick has been punching above their weight, and yet, the season always seems one injury away from being derailed.

The news that Frenkie de Jong is experiencing discomfort after playing one half of football for the Netherlands raises alarm bells for good reasons.

The return of Frenkie was a shot of adrenaline for Barcelona when they needed it most against Atletico Madrid. We all know Rodri and Pedri need rest, and the only player who can fill in without a drop in quality is the Dutchman.

The problem of depth is also huge defensively. It could be argued that, even when healthy, Barcelona doesn't have a world class backline. When your top three defenders all become sidelined for an extended time, it's a crisis that not even the best coaching, or the best attacking players, can bail you out of.

When everyone is available and rested, combined with Hansi Flick's tactics, Barcelona may very well be the best team in the world.

In reality, when it matters most, these will not be conditions that Barcelona can rely on.

A truly great team isn't made of 11 players, but rather 18 you can truly count on. From there, a great coach can manage the calendar and choose who plays when to maximize results throughout the campaign.

By now, we know Flick's gala eleven. We are also starting to see his preferred second string. Barcelona's trophies in the end, I believe, will be determined on the margins by who Flick turns to, or doesn't, as backups during critical moments of the season.

For attacking players, Flick has all the depth he needs. The question will be who he selects and when, and ultimately if he will be able to keep Raphinha and Lamine Yamal at one hundred percent for the biggest games.

Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi can continue to share time, but we have seen far too little of Gabriel Jesus and Hamza Abdelkarim. It's better to give them minutes now so they can build confidence, and so Flick can learn which of the two can be trusted to help the team while Raphinha gets much-needed rest.

I'm always skeptical of the argument that only the coach sees what's happening at training, so only he can truly know if a player will perform in games. Games are not practices. The only way you really know anything about any player is to see them in action in a high-pressure situation.

That leads me to another interesting dilemma. Marc Bernal versus Gavi. It seems that Flick is giving up on using Gavi as an option in the double pivot, and instead is using him as a third string backup behind Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo. Is this a mistake?

From what we've seen from Bernal against PSG, he doesn't make mistakes, but he also offers little in the way of positivity and creativity going forward. At times, especially in a backup role, Gavi's fighting spirit, and track record of scoring goals before his injuries, could be very valuable.

Finally, the defense. This is the area where the lack of quality depth could be most detrimental to the team's success, and where activity in the winter market is needed most.

In the meantime, with Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, and Andreas Christensen back, Hansi Flick has important decisions to make.

In La Liga, against all teams apart from Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, he can go with an attack-minded full-back like João Cancelo.

In the Champions League, and the biggest La Liga matches, I hope he rediscovers an appreciation for Jules Kounde in particular. He may not be flashy or perfect defensively, but he gives the best balance of all the qualities that are needed from a full-back in Barcelona's system at the moment.

From there, I'd love to see Eric Garcia as the Swiss Army Knife of the team again, instead of the guaranteed starter in any one position.

Rotation is the name of the game. Now more than ever, Flick must get it right.

He is the man in charge, and doing things well from a coaching perspective will require challenging his own assumptions.
